title: QueryResult
description: What the `notlob query ...` commands print to stdout with `--format json`, each a JSON value (`search`, `children`, `imports`, `imported-by`, `callers`, `callees`, `cites` and `cited-by` print text by default, a line a node). `children`, `imports`, `imported-by`, `callers`, `callees`, `cites`, `cited-by` and `search` print a NodeList (an empty array when there is nothing to list, exit code 0). `resolve` prints a NodeOrNull. `content` prints, with `--format json`, a ContentOrNull: the subtree at an address, nested and narrow (by default it prints the source as text, which is not JSON). All print `null` and exit 1 when the address or label does not resolve. A node, a reference and an edge here are the name-graph's (`GraphRef` and `Edge` are identical to `GraphRef` and `GraphEdge` in name_graph.json, and `Node` has the properties of `GraphNode`; a test keeps them so). A query prints every node with its `label` and `file`, which the graph document gives a module only, because an answer stands on its own. With no project, or an address collision that stops the graph being built, nothing is printed to stdout, an error goes to stderr, and the exit code is 1.

NodeList.description: An array of nodes, in graph order.

NodeOrNull.description: A node, or null when it does not resolve.

Content.description: A node and what it contains, down the depth asked for, nested: `children` are what the node contains, in document order. There are no edges (nesting is the containment; the other queries answer the cross-references), no label (the address carries it), no size and no references (they are written in the text). Each line of source is in the answer once: a leaf holds its `text`, and a symbol holds none unless the code block it is written in is not in the answer. The root also has its `file` and `end_line`.

kind.description: What kind of element this node is.

named.description: True where the document gives the node a name; absent otherwise.

mode.description: When a RUN runs; present on a RUN only.

declares.description: What a DECLARATION declares; present on a DECLARATION only.

value.description: The value a DECLARATION gives it, when it has one.

file.description: The .lob file the root is written in, relative to the project root, with '/' separators. On the root only.

start_line.description: 1-based line of its file where it begins.

end_line.description: 1-based last non-blank line of its file that it occupies. On the root only.

text.description: The text the node holds: a paragraph with its references written with their sigils, a dedented code block, a bullet list's items one to a line, a claim's dedented lines, a run of assertions or a named test as written. Absent on a node that holds none.

children.description: What the node contains, in document order. Absent when it contains nothing, or at the depth asked for.

ContentOrNull.description: A node's content, or null when the address does not resolve.

Node.description: One element of a .lob file: a module, a section, a paragraph, a code block, a claim, a test, a symbol, or an external file.

label.description: Human-readable name as written in source.

kind.description: What kind of element this node is.

named.description: True where the document gives the node a name (a heading, a `##group`, a `~property` or a `~test`); its `label` is the name. Absent for an anonymous node and for what a document does not name.

mode.description: When a RUN runs; present on a RUN only. A bare `~run` is `on-invocation`.

declares.description: What a DECLARATION declares; present on a DECLARATION only.

value.description: The value a DECLARATION gives it (the language, or the file), when it has one; present on a DECLARATION only.

file.description: The .lob file it is written in, relative to the project root, with '/' separators. Absent for an external file and for a module built on its own.

start_line.description: 1-based line of its file where it begins.

end_line.description: 1-based last non-blank line of its file that it occupies.

size.description: The characters of text held at or under the node, each leaf's text counted once; a symbol holds none of its own, so it adds nothing to its section and its own size is that of its lines. Present from `index` on.

refs.description: The references a paragraph holds, in the order written. Present on a PROSE node from `index` on.

text.description: The text the node holds: a paragraph with its references written with their sigils, a dedented code block, a bullet list's items one to a line, a claim's dedented lines, a run of assertions or a named test as written. Present at `full` on each node that holds text, and never on a symbol (its lines are in its code block).

GraphRef.description: A `#Label` or `##Label` written in a paragraph.

label.description: What it names, without the sigil.

sub.description: True for `##Label`, which names a subheading of the module only.

Edge.description: A directed relationship between two nodes.

kind.description: CONTAINS: a node to what is written in it (the trees); CITES: a paragraph to the node a `#Label` in it names; USES: code to a symbol it refers to by name; IMPORTS: a module to a module it lists in #References; USES_EXTERNAL: the binding module to a file it declares.

start_line.description: 1-based line of the source's file of the first reference or call site, where the edge has one. Where edges are merged, the earliest.
